prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world the agent's observation shows the target shifted: the target, missing, extra and target-height channels are rolled 4 columns toward higher x, wrapping around. The world, its designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
No trials have run yet. The starting network learned to pick DONE at once on every episode. Its traces show why: the target heights the agent observed are the true design shifted cyclically by X/2 columns. For example, design row 1 '00220000' was observed as '00000022', and this holds on every row of both designs. So the world misaligns the target channels, and the 'missing' and 'extra' channels may be affected too. A stack of two 3x3 convolutions can't see 4 columns away, so it can't line up the target with the build. Random placements earn negative reward, which teaches the agent that DONE (reward 0) is the best move. I don't know if the build channels are also shifted, or if the y axis is affected on other grid sizes. Each candidate therefore gives the network a learned way to mix information across the whole grid, rather than hard-coding the shift: learned per-channel mixing along each axis, or attention over cells with positional encodings. A third candidate also tests a recipe that runs more PPO updates.

### Round 2
The diagnostic traces show the observed target is the real design shifted cyclically by X/2 along x only. Rows match, and design column c appears at column c+X/2. A purely local CNN (the starting net) cannot line up the target with the build, and it collapses to choosing DONE before any placement. Learned axial mixing (r1c1) was the only trial to escape: 0.047 on one seed and 0.004 on the other. On seed 0 it nearly collapsed mid-run (mean episode length 1.6 at 50%) and then recovered. Its twin with a different recipe (r1c3) collapsed completely, so collapse to DONE is a seed-luck problem layered on the alignment problem. When r1c1 does place bricks, it places them almost entirely inside the target (16 cells inside vs 0.2 outside per episode) and then stops too early. Next steps: give the network the alignment directly by concatenating an input copy rolled by X/2 (allowed as slice plus concatenate), and reduce the pull toward DONE.

### Round 3
The observed target, height and missing/extra channels are shifted cyclically by X/2 along x; the traces confirm this. Everything that works undoes the shift. Axial mixing alone scored 0.025 and was unstable. Adding the rolled target copy (r2c1) raised it to 0.48, and the two seeds agree (0.49 and 0.47), so the gain is far larger than seed noise. r2c3 (roll, no axial mixing, more FLOPs and fewer samples) scored 0.13, so the axial mixing and/or the sample count matter. A gentler recipe (r2c2: lower lr, more entropy) hurt badly (0.11), which says learning speed is the bottleneck. r2c1's training success was still climbing steeply at the end (0.20 at 75%, 0.35 at 100%), so it is short of samples. Its greedy failures stop early (DONE) on taller columns of 2–3 layers and leave missing cells. That points to weak credit for the exact-build bonus and to under-training. This round keeps r2c1's network and tests two things: more samples per FLOP (fewer PPO epochs) and longer-horizon credit (higher gamma and lambda).

### Round 4
The observed target is shifted cyclically by X/2 along x, so it does not line up with the build. Adding a copy of the target rolled back by X/2 (r2c1, 0.48) was the breakthrough. Without it, runs collapse to DONE. The rest of the gain came from more samples per FLOP. With 2 PPO epochs, r3c1 reached 0.76 (0.82 and 0.69). With 1 epoch and 64-sample minibatches, r3c3 averaged 0.50, but its seeds diverged: 0.91 and 0.08. One epoch can reach a higher score but is unstable. Its seed-0 training success reached 0.89 and was still rising. Lower lr with more entropy (r2c2) slowed learning. Higher gamma (r3c2) hurt and made the agent stop early. In this last round I try to make the high-sample regime stable. Two levers: larger minibatches (less gradient noise) and a zero-initialised policy output (uniform start, less early drift toward DONE). One candidate isolates zero-init on the 2-epoch best.

## Trial it ended with
name: r2c1 + 2 PPO epochs
hypothesis: Same network as r2c1, with ppo_epochs 2 instead of 4. Under the budget formula this gives about 1.86x more environment steps (about 190k), with a similar total number of gradient steps. r2c1's curve was still climbing steeply, so fresh designs should help more than reusing old samples. Refuted if the mean is below about 0.42, or if any seed collapses to DONE.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).
